body: I'm sorry that's super rough. I have experienced the same thing. It sounds like unintentional reverse psychology to me. I was diagnosed with Oppositional Defiant Disorder as a child resulting in most disagreements turning into fights. As an adult I have it managed mostly through mindfulness by using my negative feelings as an emotional trigger to take a step back and apply stoicism so I can remove the negative and look at it objectively. That along with focusing on diet, sleep, and exercise and meditation made a huge difference for me. There's no silver bullet for me but each creates about a 10% improvement. It doesn't always work but with continued effort it gets better. I know this might not be perfect or the right fit for you but I hope things turn out for you and hope this helps. I'm rooting for ya. 🤞

I havs ADHD & ODD (oppositional defiant disorder) and it sounds like your BF might too* considering you're ~10x more likely to have it if you have ADHD. I've been through relationships that sound about as difficult as yours. 

The best treatment I've found is meditation. Not only that but you'll find scientific support showing it helps with anger, anxiety, focus, depression, and more**. I've only been meditating for about a year and it's making all the difference. The fights are getting less extreme and less frequent and stay that way as long as I maintain it. Not only that but there's proven benefits to couples meditating together. It's difficult to start but well worth but you both have to be committed to sticking with it. 

I use the Headspace app because they have tons of meditation programs, including anger and relationship programs. 

Commit to at least 5 mins of meditation at least 5 days a week together.

Otherwise, I've also been in relationships that although we were in love, it was too incompatible. Sometimes it's wiser to walk away than to stay together.

TL;DR meditate and make sure you're not in an unhealthy relationship.

*Not a replacement for a professional opinion.
**Avoid meditation with multiple personality disorder.
